summary.text: Mike Haridopolos is the Republican incumbent seeking a second term in Florida's 8th Congressional District. A former college instructor, he served in the Florida House and Senate, including as Senate President from 2010 to 2012, and later ran a business and political consulting company. He was first elected to Congress in 2024.

paragraphs.text: Earned a B.A. from Stetson University in 1992, an M.A. from the University of Arkansas in 1993, and a Ph.D. from the University of Arkansas in 1999.

Began his career teaching U.S. history and political science at Brevard Community College (now Eastern Florida State College) and taught as an instructor at the Bob Graham Center at the University of Florida; he is also an author.
Served in the Florida House of Representatives (2000-2003) and the Florida State Senate (2003-2012), representing Brevard County communities.
According to his official bio, he led an effort to put the state budget online and sponsored a 2008 constitutional amendment on property taxes and homestead portability.
Served as President of the Florida Senate from 2010 to 2012.
After leaving the legislature in 2012, started a business and political consulting company.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2024, succeeding retiring Rep. Bill Posey; took office in January 2025.
Serves on the House Financial Services Committee and the Science, Space, and Technology Committee, where he chairs the Space and Aeronautics Subcommittee.
According to his official bio, lives in Indian Harbour Beach with his wife, Dr. Stephanie Haridopolos; they have three adult children.
